text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position of less than 425 mm, the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.1. shall be applied.
condition: lower bumper height at the test position less than 425 mm

text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position greater than, or equal to, 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the requirements of either paragraph 5.1.1. or 5.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer, shall be applied.
condition: lower bumper height at the test position >= 425 mm and < 500 mm

text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position greater than, or equal to, 500 mm, the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.2. shall be applied.
condition: lower bumper height at the test position >= 500 mm

text: When tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.
condition: flexible lower legform to bumper test applies

text: When tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
condition: flexible lower legform to bumper test applies

text: When tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the maximum dynamic posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
condition: flexible lower legform to bumper test applies

text: When tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.
condition: flexible lower legform to bumper test applies

text: The manufacturer may nominate bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total where the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm.
condition: if the manufacturer nominates relaxation zones and the Contracting Party does not restrict the relaxation zone requirement

text: The flexible lower legform impactor shall be certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 1.
When tested with the upper legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2., the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
condition: upper legform to bumper test applies

text: When tested with the upper legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2., the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
condition: upper legform to bumper test applies

text: The upper legform impactor shall be certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 2.

When tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3., 4. and 5., the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined bonnet top test area and windscreen test area.
The HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two-thirds of the bonnet top test area.
The HIC for the remaining test areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both child and adult headforms.

Measuring points located in the cowl monitoring area shall not be taken into consideration to assess the headform performance requirements; their results are used for monitoring only and do not contribute to the one-third and two-third area calculation.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area.
condition: only a child headform test area exists

text: In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC for the remaining area shall not exceed 1,700.
condition: only a child headform test area exists

text: When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3. and 4., the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area.
When tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3. and 4., the HIC for the remaining areas of the child headform test area shall not exceed 1,700.
The child and adult headform impactors shall be certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 3.

For a vehicle fitted with an ARHSS which could change the vehicle height at the front axle more than 20 mm from the nominal for any vehicle speed between 25 and 40 km/h, the provisions of paragraphs 5.1. and 5.2. shall, in addition to the normal running condition for 40 km/h, be met for all adjustable vehicle steady heights corresponding to vehicle speeds from 25 up to 40 km/h.
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS changing front axle height more than 20 mm from nominal between 25 and 40 km/h

text: For the ARHSS tests, on request of the manufacturer and agreed by the technical service, either the impact speeds defined in paragraphs 5.1. and 5.2. or the impact speed corresponding to the adjusted vehicle height shall be used.
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS subject to paragraph 5.3

text: Where the impact speed corresponding to the adjusted vehicle height is used, the ratio of the head impact speed vs. the corresponding vehicle velocity shall be 0.9.
condition: impact speed corresponding to the adjusted vehicle height is used

text: The requirements of paragraph 5.3. are deemed fulfilled only if the ARHSS fully corresponds to the conditions of paragraph 5.3.1.1. or 5.3.1.2.
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS

text: The ARHSS cannot be activated on public roads and is activated for off-road use only.
condition: compliance claimed via paragraph 5.3.1.1

text: The ARHSS returns automatically to the normal ride attitude when the vehicle is operating on public roads.
condition: compliance claimed via paragraph 5.3.1.1

text: The default status of the ARHSS on public roads is the normal ride height at the initiation of each new engine start/run cycle.
condition: compliance claimed via paragraph 5.3.1.1

text: An ARHSS engaged for exceptional low speed use cases on public roads shall automatically return to the normal ride height when the vehicle speed exceeds 25 km/h.
condition: ARHSS engageable for exceptional low speed use cases on public roads

text: An ARHSS engaged for exceptional low speed use cases on public roads shall automatically return to the normal ride height when the system is manually disengaged by the driver.
condition: ARHSS engageable for exceptional low speed use cases on public roads

text: Engagement of an ARHSS for exceptional low speed use cases is indicated to the driver at least by an optical warning signal.
condition: ARHSS for exceptional low speed use cases is engaged

text: Compliance with the conditions of paragraph 5.3.1.1. or 5.3.1.2. shall be demonstrated by the vehicle manufacturer to the satisfaction of the technical service by independent means (e.g. a physical test).
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS

text: The relevant information on the ARHSS conditions shall be described in the information document in Annex 1.
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS

text: The exceptional low speed use case of paragraph 5.3.1.2 shall be additionally described in the owner's handbook.
condition: ARHSS for exceptional low speed use cases

text: The legform impactor used for ARHSS tests shall be the legform impactor as used for the legform to bumper test in normal running conditions for a speed of 40 km/h.
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS subject to paragraph 5.3

text: With the agreement of the technical service, compliance for ARHSS heights shall be demonstrated by a limited number of legform tests or by numerical simulation so that the biomechanical limits of paragraphs 5.1.1. and 5.1.2. respectively are met.
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS subject to paragraph 5.3

text: With the agreement of the technical service, compliance shall be demonstrated by a limited number of head impact tests or by numerical simulation showing compliance to the HIC 1,700 requirement on the additional head test area.
condition: vehicle fitted with an ARHSS subject to paragraph 5.3

text: Procedures concerning conformity of production shall conform to the general provisions defined in the Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
A vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5.

The Type Approval Authority which has granted approval may at any time verify the conformity of control methods applicable to each production unit; the normal frequency of such inspections shall be once every two years.
The information document information shall be supplied in triplicate and include a list of contents.
Any drawings in the information document shall be supplied in appropriate scale and in sufficient detail on size A4 or on a folder of A4 format.
Photographs in the information document, if any, shall show sufficient details.
condition: if photographs are supplied

text: If the systems, components or separate technical units have electronic controls, information concerning their performance shall be supplied.
condition: systems, components or separate technical units have electronic controls

text: If the means of identification of type contains characters not relevant to describe the vehicle type, such characters shall be represented in the documentation by the symbol "?".
condition: means of identification of type contains non-relevant characters

text: The information document shall state make, type, commercial names, means of identification of type and its location, vehicle category, name and address of manufacturer, assembly plants and manufacturer's representative.

A detailed description, including photographs and/or drawings, of the vehicle with respect to the structure, the dimensions, the relevant reference lines and the constituent materials of the frontal part of the vehicle (interior and exterior) shall be provided.
The description shall include detail of any active protection system installed.
condition: if an active protection system is installed

text: The description shall include detail of any system which could change the vehicle height at the front axle while driving (e.g. ARHSS).
condition: if such a system is fitted

text: The communication form shall report cowl monitoring area results (point, WAD, Y-coordinate, impact speed, HIC value) and whether the WAD 2,100 boundary is applicable.
The communication form shall report monitoring results for areas incorporating pedestrian or bicyclist head injury mitigation features on A-pillar, windscreen header and cowl.
condition: if applicable

text: The communication form shall report manufacturer-requested impact points on innovative solutions on A-pillar, windscreen header and cowl.
condition: if applicable

text: The approval mark shall be arranged as in the model of Annex 2, with dimension a of at least 8 mm.
At the time of testing, the test facility and the vehicle or sub-system shall have a relative humidity of 40 per cent ± 30 per cent.
At the time of testing, the test facility and the vehicle or sub-system shall have a stabilized temperature of 20 ºC ± 4 ºC.
The impact test site shall consist of a flat, smooth and hard surface with a slope not exceeding 1 per cent.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body, adjusted to the conditions of Annex 3 paragraph 3.1., shall be used for the test.
The test vehicle shall be in its normal ride attitude and either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.
condition: complete vehicle tested

text: The cut-body shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure, all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user.
condition: cut-body tested

text: The cut-body shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.
condition: cut-body tested

text: All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The manufacturer shall show that any devices to protect vulnerable road users will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

Vehicle components which could change shape or position, other than active devices to protect pedestrians, and which have more than one fixed shape or position, shall require the vehicle to comply with the components in each fixed shape or position.
condition: components with more than one fixed shape or position

text: The flexible lower legform impactor shall consist of flesh and skin, flexible long bone segments (representing femur and tibia), and a knee joint as shown in Figure 1.
The assembled flexible lower legform impactor shall have a total mass of 13.2 kg ± 0.4 kg.

The dimensions of the fully assembled flexible lower legform impactor shall be as defined in Figure 1; brackets, pulleys, protectors, connection parts, etc. for launching and/or protection may extend beyond these dimensions and tolerances.
The cross-sectional shape of the femur main body segments, the tibia main body segments and their impact faces shall be as defined in Figure 2(a).
The cross-sectional shape of the knee joint and its impact face shall be as defined in Figure 2(b).
The mass of the femur without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts to the knee joint, shall be 2.46 kg ± 0.12 kg.
The mass of the tibia without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts to the knee joint, shall be 2.64 kg ± 0.13 kg.
The mass of the knee joint without the flesh and skin shall be 4.28 kg ± 0.21 kg.
The assembled mass of the femur, the knee joint and the tibia without the flesh and skin shall be 9.38 kg ± 0.3 kg.
The centres of gravity of the femur and tibia without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts to the knee joint, shall be as defined in Figure 1.
The centre of gravity of the knee joint shall be as defined in Figure 1.

The moment of inertia of the femur without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts inserted to the knee joint, about the X-axis through its centre of gravity shall be 0.0339 kgm² ± 0.0016 kgm².

The moment of inertia of the tibia without the flesh and skin, including the connection parts inserted to the knee joint, about the X-axis through its centre of gravity shall be 0.0486 kgm² ± 0.0023 kgm².
The moment of inertia of the knee joint about the X-axis through its centre of gravity shall be 0.0180 kgm² ± 0.0009 kgm².
Four transducers shall be installed in the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor to measure bending moments at the locations within the tibia defined in Figure 2.
Three transducers shall be installed in the femur of the flexible lower legform impactor to measure bending moments applied to the femur.
The measurement axis of each femur and tibia transducer shall be the X-axis of the impactor.
Three transducers shall be installed in the knee joint to measure elongations of the MCL, ACL and PCL, at the locations shown in Figure 3.
The knee ligament measurement locations shall be within ±4 mm along the X-axis from the knee joint centre.
The instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all flexible lower legform impactor transducers.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 400 Nm for the tibia and femur bending moments.
The determination of all flexible lower legform impactor peak tibia bending moments and ligament elongations shall be limited to the assessment interval (AI) as defined in paragraph 2.2.
The upper legform impactor shall be rigid, foam covered at the impact side, and 350 mm ± 5 mm long.
The total mass of the upper legform impactor including those propulsion and guidance components which are effectively part of the impactor during the impact shall be 9.5 kg ± 0.1 kg.

The total mass of the front member and other components in front of the load transducer assemblies, together with those parts of the load transducer assemblies in front of the active elements, but excluding the foam and skin, shall be 1.95 kg ± 0.05 kg.
The upper legform impactor for the bumper test shall be mounted to the propulsion system by a torque limiting joint and be insensitive to off-axis loading.

The upper legform impactor shall move only in the specified direction of impact when in contact with the vehicle and shall be prevented from motion in other directions including rotation about any axis.
The torque limiting joint shall be set so that the longitudinal axis of the front member is vertical at the time of impact with a tolerance of ±2°.
The joint friction torque of the upper legform torque limiting joint shall be set to 675 Nm ± 25 Nm.

The centre of gravity of those parts of the upper legform impactor effectively forward of the torque limiting joint, including any weights fitted, shall lie on the longitudinal centre line of the impactor, with a tolerance of ±10 mm.
The length between the load transducer centre lines of the upper legform impactor shall be 310 mm ± 1 mm.
The front member diameter of the upper legform impactor shall be 50 mm ± 1 mm.
The front member of the upper legform impactor shall be strain gauged to measure bending moments in three positions, as shown in Figure 4, each using a separate channel.
The strain gauges of the upper legform impactor are located on the back of the front member; the two outer strain gauges are located 50 mm ± 1 mm from the impactor's symmetrical axis.
The middle strain gauge of the upper legform impactor is located on the symmetrical axis with a ±1 mm tolerance.
Two load transducers shall be fitted to measure individually the forces applied at either end of the upper legform impactor.
Strain gauges shall be fitted measuring bending moments at the centre of the upper legform impactor and at positions 50 mm either side of the centre line (see Figure 4).
The instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers of the upper legform impactor.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 10 kN for the force transducers of the upper legform impactor.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 1,000 Nm for the bending moment measurements of the upper legform impactor.
The child headform impactor shall be made of aluminium, be of homogenous construction and be of spherical shape.
The overall diameter of the child headform impactor shall be 165 mm ± 1 mm.
The mass of the child headform impactor shall be 3.5 kg ± 0.07 kg.
The moment of inertia of the child headform impactor about an axis through the centre of gravity and perpendicular to the direction of impact shall be within the range of 0.008 to 0.012 kgm2.
The centre of gravity of the child headform impactor including instrumentation shall be located in the geometric centre of the sphere with a tolerance of ±2 mm.
The child headform impactor sphere shall be covered with a 14 mm ± 0.5 mm thick synthetic skin, which shall cover at least half of the sphere.
The first natural frequency of the child headform impactor shall be over 5,000 Hz.

A recess in the child headform sphere shall allow for mounting one triaxial or three uniaxial accelerometers within ±10 mm seismic mass location tolerance from the centre of the sphere for the measurement axis, and ±1 mm seismic mass location tolerance from the centre of the sphere for the perpendicular direction to the measurement axis.

One of the uniaxial accelerometers of the child headform impactor shall have its sensitive axis perpendicular to the mounting face A (see Figure 5) and its seismic mass shall be positioned within a cylindrical tolerance field of 1 mm radius and 20 mm length.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The centre line of the cylindrical tolerance field of the child headform accelerometer shall run perpendicular to the mounting face and its mid-point shall coincide with the centre of the sphere of the headform impactor.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The remaining accelerometers of the child headform impactor shall have their sensitive axes perpendicular to each other and parallel to the mounting face A and their seismic mass shall be positioned within a spherical tolerance field of 10 mm radius.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The centre of the spherical tolerance field of the remaining child headform accelerometers shall coincide with the centre of the sphere of the headform impactor.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The instrumentation response value CFC of the child headform impactor, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 1,000.
The CAC response value of the child headform impactor, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 500 g for the acceleration.
The adult headform impactor shall be made of aluminium, be of homogenous construction and be of spherical shape.
The overall diameter of the adult headform impactor is 165 mm ± 1 mm as shown in Figure 6.
The mass of the adult headform impactor shall be 4.5 kg ± 0.1 kg.
The moment of inertia of the adult headform impactor about an axis through the centre of gravity and perpendicular to the direction of impact shall be within the range of 0.010 to 0.013 kgm2.
The centre of gravity of the adult headform impactor including instrumentation shall be located in the geometric centre of the sphere with a tolerance of ±5 mm.
The adult headform impactor sphere shall be covered with a 14 mm ± 0.5 mm thick synthetic skin, which shall cover at least half of the sphere.
The first natural frequency of the adult headform impactor shall be over 5,000 Hz.

A recess in the adult headform sphere shall allow for mounting one triaxial or three uniaxial accelerometers within ±10 mm seismic mass location tolerance from the centre of the sphere for the measurement axis, and ±1 mm seismic mass location tolerance from the centre of the sphere for the perpendicular direction to the measurement axis.

One of the uniaxial accelerometers of the adult headform impactor shall have its sensitive axis perpendicular to the mounting face A (see Figure 6) and its seismic mass shall be positioned within a cylindrical tolerance field of 1 mm radius and 20 mm length.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The centre line of the cylindrical tolerance field of the adult headform accelerometer shall run perpendicular to the mounting face and its mid-point shall coincide with the centre of the sphere of the headform impactor.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The remaining accelerometers of the adult headform impactor shall have their sensitive axes perpendicular to each other and parallel to the mounting face A and their seismic mass shall be positioned within a spherical tolerance field of 10 mm radius.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The centre of the spherical tolerance field of the remaining adult headform accelerometers shall coincide with the centre of the sphere of the headform impactor.
condition: if three uniaxial accelerometers are used

text: The instrumentation response value CFC of the adult headform impactor, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 1,000.
The CAC response value of the adult headform impactor, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 500 g for the acceleration.

A rear flat face shall be provided on the outer surface of the child and adult headform impactors which is perpendicular to the direction of travel, and typically perpendicular to the axis of one of the accelerometers, being a flat plate capable of providing for access to the accelerometers and an attachment point for the propulsion system.

For each test the flexible lower legform impactor (femur, knee joint and tibia) shall be covered by flesh and skin composed of synthetic rubber sheets (R1, R2) and neoprene sheets (N1F, N2F, N1T, N2T, N3) as shown in Figure 1.
The size of the flesh and skin sheets of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be within the requirements described in Figure 1.
The flesh and skin sheets of the flexible lower legform impactor are required to have compression characteristics as shown in Figure 2.
The compression characteristics shall be checked using material from the same batch as the sheets used for the flexible lower legform impactor flesh and skin.

All flexible lower legform impactor components shall be stored for a sufficient period of time in a controlled storage area with a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C prior to impactor removal for testing.
After removal from the storage the flexible lower legform impactor shall not be subjected to conditions other than those pertaining in the test area as defined in Annex 3, paragraph 1.1.
Each flexible lower legform test shall be completed within two hours of when the impactor to be used is removed from the controlled storage area.
The selected measuring points for the flexible lower legform test shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14.
A minimum of three lower legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.
Lower legform to bumper tests shall be to different types of structure, where they vary throughout the area to be assessed.
The selected lower legform test points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart as measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
The lower legform positions tested by the laboratories shall be indicated in the test report.

The direction of the impact velocity vector of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±2° in the horizontal plane and in the longitudinal plane at the time of first contact.
The axis of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane with a roll and pitch angle tolerance of ±2° in the lateral and longitudinal plane.

The bottom of the flexible lower legform impactor (without parts needed for the purposes of launching and/or protection) shall be at 75 mm above ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper, with a ±10 mm tolerance.
When setting the height of the propulsion system, an allowance shall be made for the influence of gravity during the period of free flight of the flexible lower legform impactor.
The lower legform impactor for the bumper tests shall be in free flight at the moment of impact.

The lower legform impactor shall be released to free flight at such a distance from the vehicle that the test results are not influenced by contact of the impactor with the propulsion system during rebound of the impactor.
The lower legform impactor may be propelled by any means only if it can be shown to meet the requirements of the test.

At the time of first contact the flexible lower legform impactor shall have the intended orientation about its vertical axis, for the correct operation of its knee joint, with a yaw angle tolerance of ±5°.
For the lower legform testing, a horizontal and vertical impact tolerance of ±10 mm shall apply.
During contact between the flexible lower legform impactor and the vehicle, the impactor shall not contact the ground or any object which is not part of the vehicle.
The impact velocity of the flexible lower legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
The effect of gravity shall be taken into account when the impact velocity of the flexible lower legform impactor is obtained from measurements taken before the time of first contact.
condition: when impact velocity is obtained from measurements taken before first contact

text: The tibia bending moments of the flexible lower legform impactor shall not exceed +/- 15 Nm within an evaluation interval of 30 ms immediately prior to impact.
The offset compensation shall be done with the flexible lower legform impactor in resting position prior to the test/acceleration phase.
For each upper legform test the foam flesh shall be two new sheets of 25 mm thick foam type CF-45 or equivalent, cut from the sheet of material used for the dynamic certification test.
The skin of the upper legform impactor shall be a 1.5 mm thick fibre reinforced rubber sheet.

The mass of the foam and the rubber skin of the upper legform impactor together shall be 0.6 kg ± 0.1 kg (excluding any reinforcement, mountings, etc. used to attach the rear edges of the rubber skin to the rear member).

The foam and rubber skin of the upper legform impactor shall be folded back towards the rear, with the rubber skin attached via spacers to the rear member so that the sides of the rubber skin are held parallel.

The foam of the upper legform impactor shall be of such a size and shape that an adequate gap is maintained between the foam and components behind the front member, to avoid significant load paths between the foam and these components.

The upper legform test impactor or at least the foam flesh shall be stored during a period of at least four hours in a controlled storage area with a stabilized humidity of 35 per cent ± 15 per cent and a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C prior to impactor removal for test.
After removal from the storage the upper legform impactor shall not be subjected to conditions other than those pertaining in the test area.
Each upper legform test shall be completed within two hours of when the impactor to be used is removed from the controlled storage area.
The selected measuring points for the upper legform test shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14.
A minimum of three upper legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.
Upper legform to bumper tests shall be to different types of structure, where they vary throughout the area to be assessed.
The selected upper legform measuring points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart as measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
The upper legform positions tested by the laboratories shall be indicated in the test report.

The direction of impact of the upper legform impactor shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, with the axis of the upper legform vertical at the time of first contact, with a tolerance of ±2°.
At the time of first contact the upper legform impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line with a ±10 mm tolerance.
At the time of first contact the upper legform impactor vertical centre line shall be positioned laterally with the selected impact location with a tolerance of ±10 mm.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
The headform impactors shall be in free flight at the moment of impact, at the required impact velocity (paragraphs 4.6. and 5.6.) and the required direction of impact (paragraphs 4.7. and 5.7.).

The headform impactors shall be released to free flight at such a distance from the vehicle that the test results are not influenced by contact of the impactor with the propulsion system during rebound of the impactor.
The velocity of the headform impactor shall be measured at some point during the free flight before impact, in accordance with the method specified in ISO 3784:1976.

The measured headform velocity shall be adjusted considering all factors which may affect the impactor between the point of measurement and the point of impact, in order to determine the velocity of the impactor at the time of impact.
The angle of the headform velocity vector at the time of impact shall be calculated or measured.
The headform acceleration time histories shall be recorded, and HIC shall be calculated.
The measuring point on the front structure of the vehicle shall be recorded for each headform test.
Recording of headform test results shall be in accordance with ISO 6487:2002.
The manufacturer shall identify the zones of the bonnet top test area and of the windscreen test area where the HIC shall not exceed 1,000 (HIC1000 zone) or 1,700 (HIC1700 zone).

Marking of the bonnet top test area, the windscreen test area and the HIC1000 zone and HIC1700 zone shall be based on a drawing supplied by the manufacturer, viewed from a horizontal plane above the vehicle parallel to the vehicle horizontal zero plane.

A sufficient number of x and y co-ordinates shall be supplied by the manufacturer to mark up the bonnet top, windscreen, HIC1000 and HIC1700 areas on the actual vehicle while considering the vehicle outer contour in the z direction.
The cowl monitoring area shall not be considered for the marking of the HIC1000 zone and HIC1700 zone.
The determination of the impacted HIC1000 or HIC1700 zone is done by the measuring point; the zones may consist of several parts with the number of parts not limited.

The calculation of the surface of the bonnet top test area, of the windscreen test area and of the HIC1000 zone and HIC1700 zone shall be done on the basis of a projected bonnet and windscreen viewed from a horizontal plane parallel to the horizontal zero plane above the vehicle, on the basis of the drawing data supplied by the manufacturer.

Less than nine headform tests for each impactor may be performed only if a number of measuring points have been selected in order of potential to cause injury and the test area remaining is too small to select another measuring point while maintaining the minimum spacing between points.
condition: remaining test area too small for another measuring point at minimum spacing

text: The headform positions tested by the laboratories shall be indicated in the test report.

The technical services conducting the tests shall perform as many headform tests as necessary to guarantee the compliance of the vehicle with the HIC limit values of 1,000 for the HIC1000 zone and 1,700 for the HIC1700 zone, especially in the points near to the borders between the two types of zones.
Child headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries of the child headform bonnet top test area as defined in paragraph 2.16.
Child headform tests shall also be made to the windscreen within the boundaries of the windscreen test area as defined in paragraph 2.44.
For child headform tests on the rear area of the bonnet top, the headform impactor shall not contact the windscreen or A-pillar before impacting the bonnet top.
condition: for tests on the rear area of the bonnet top

text: For child headform tests on the windscreen, the headform impactor shall not directly contact the A-pillars, windscreen header and cowl, except in the case of monitoring testing.
condition: for tests on the windscreen, except monitoring testing

text: A minimum of nine tests shall be carried out with the child headform impactor over the child bonnet top test area and the child windscreen test area together, with three tests each to the middle and the outer thirds of the child/small adult test areas, at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.
Where possible, at least one of the nine child headform tests shall be carried out on the windscreen test area.
condition: where possible

text: At the discretion of the technical service, one of the nine child headform tests may be conducted in the cowl monitoring area.
condition: at the discretion of the technical service

text: For each child headform test on the windscreen an undamaged and untested windscreen shall be used.
condition: for each test on the windscreen

text: Child headform tests shall be to different types of structure, where these vary throughout the area to be assessed, and at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.
condition: where structure types vary throughout the area to be assessed

text: Taking into account any symmetry of the windscreen and relevant structures, the number of child headform tests on the windscreen test area may be reduced at the discretion of the Technical Service.
condition: symmetry of the windscreen and relevant structures, at discretion of the Technical Service

text: The selected measuring points for the child/small adult headform impactor shall be a minimum of 165 mm apart, set with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.
The selected measuring points for the child/small adult headform impactor shall be within the child headform test areas as defined in paragraphs 2.16. and 2.44.
No child headform measuring point shall be located so that the impactor will impact the test area with a glancing blow resulting in a more severe second impact outside the test area.
For the child headform testing, a longitudinal and transversal impact tolerance of ±10 mm, measured along the surface of the bonnet or the windscreen, shall apply.
The test laboratory may verify at a sufficient number of measuring points that the ±10 mm child headform impact tolerance can be met.
The child headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
The direction of impact of the child headform shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle to be tested at an angle of 50° ± 2° to the horizontal.
The direction of impact of child headform tests to the front structure shall be downward and rearward.
condition: tests to the front structure

text: Child headform tests may be repeated in case of atypical windscreen fracture at the manufacturer's request where the HIC value exceeds or is equal to the respective limit of the head impact zone, with a maximum of 3 repetitions on a measuring point (i.e. 4 tests total).
condition: in case of atypical windscreen fracture and HIC equal to or above the zone limit

text: On request of the technical service, child headform tests with atypical windscreen fracture may be repeated where the HIC value is below the limit of the head impact zone, for instance in case of underlying structures within 100 mm of the measuring point.
condition: atypical windscreen fracture and HIC below the zone limit, on request of the technical service

text: Child headform tests with atypical windscreen fracture shall be duly recorded in the test report.
condition: in case of atypical windscreen fracture

text: Pedestrian or bicyclist head injury mitigation features incorporated in the A-pillars and/or windscreen header (e.g. external airbag, deployable structure, energy absorption elements) shall be declared by the manufacturer.
condition: if the A-pillars and/or windscreen header incorporate head injury mitigation features

text: If the A-pillars and/or windscreen header incorporate pedestrian or bicyclist head injury mitigation features, additional child headform monitoring tests shall be carried out on such structure.
condition: if the A-pillars and/or windscreen header incorporate head injury mitigation features, unless the Contracting Party indicates monitoring results are not required

text: The measuring points for monitoring tests on the A-pillars, windscreen header and/or cowl shall be selected as agreed between the technical service and the manufacturer so that the effectiveness of the protection can be scientifically assessed; the prescribed clearance distances or exclusion areas need not be observed.
condition: for monitoring tests

text: The vehicle manufacturer may voluntarily request child headform monitoring tests in case of any other innovative solutions that reduce head injury levels in case of head contact with A-pillars and/or windscreen header.
condition: on manufacturer request for innovative solutions

text: The child headform monitoring results shall be detailed in point 16 of the type-approval communication form.
condition: if monitoring tests are carried out

text: A detailed description of the protective system, the selected measuring points and the results of the assessment shall be included in the information document.
condition: if monitoring tests are carried out

text: Adult headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries of the adult headform bonnet top test area as defined in paragraph 2.1.
Adult headform tests shall also be made to the windscreen within the boundaries of the windscreen test area as defined in paragraph 2.44.
For adult headform tests at the rear of the bonnet top, the headform impactor shall not contact the windscreen or A-pillar before impacting the bonnet top.
condition: for tests at the rear of the bonnet top

text: For adult headform tests on the windscreen, the headform impactor shall not directly contact the A-pillars, windscreen header and cowl, except in the case of monitoring testing.
condition: for tests on the windscreen, except monitoring testing

text: A minimum of nine tests shall be carried out with the adult headform impactor over the adult bonnet top test area and the adult windscreen test area together, with three tests each to the middle and the outer thirds of the adult test areas, at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.
Where possible, at least one of the nine adult headform tests shall be carried out on the windscreen test area.
condition: where possible

text: At the discretion of the technical service, one of the nine adult headform tests may be conducted in the cowl monitoring area.
condition: at the discretion of the technical service

text: For each adult headform test on the windscreen an undamaged and untested windscreen shall be used.
condition: for each test on the windscreen

text: Adult headform tests shall be to different types of structure, where these vary throughout the area to be assessed, and at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.
condition: where structure types vary throughout the area to be assessed

text: Taking into account any symmetry of the windscreen and relevant structures, the number of adult headform tests on the windscreen test area may be reduced at the discretion of the Technical Service.

text: The flexible lower legform impactor shall be certified according to the inverse certification (IC) test procedure of paragraph 1.4. before starting a vehicle test series.
After a maximum of 10 vehicle tests, the flexible lower legform impactor should be certified according to the pendulum certification (PC) test procedure of paragraph 1.3.
Ongoing certification testing of the flexible lower legform impactor shall constitute the sequence IC - PC - PC - IC - PC - PC - etc. with a maximum of 10 tests between each certification.
The flexible lower legform impactor shall be certified according to the static certification procedures of paragraph 1.2. at least once a year.
The femur and the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor shall meet the requirements of paragraph 1.2.2. when tested according to paragraph 1.2.4.
The knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor shall meet the requirements of paragraph 1.2.3. when tested according to paragraph 1.2.5.
The stabilized temperature of the flexible lower legform impactor during the static certification tests shall be 20 °C ± 2 °C.
In the static certification tests, the CAC response values, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations and 4 kN for the applied external load.

For the static certification tests, low-pass filtering at an appropriate frequency is permitted only to remove higher frequency noise without significantly affecting the measurement of the response of the impactor.

When the femur and the tibia of the flexible lower legform impactor are loaded in bending in accordance with paragraph 1.2.4., the applied moment and the generated deflection at the centre of the femur and the tibia (Mc and Dc) shall be within the corridors shown in Figure 1.

When the knee joint of the flexible lower legform impactor is loaded in bending in accordance with paragraph 1.2.5., the MCL, ACL and PCL elongations and applied bending moment or the force at the centre of the knee joint (Mc or Fc) shall be within the corridors shown in Figure 2.
In the femur and tibia static certification test, the edges of the femur and tibia, not bending parts, shall be mounted to the support rig firmly as shown in Figure 3 and Figure 4.
In the femur and tibia static certification test, the Y-axis of the impactor shall be parallel to the loading axis within 180° ± 2° tolerance.
In the femur and tibia static certification test, the centre of the loading force shall be applied at the centre of the femur and the tibia within ±2 mm tolerance along the Z-axis.

In the femur and tibia static certification test, the force shall be increased so as to maintain a deflection rate between 10 and 100 mm/minute until the bending moment at the centre part (Mc) of the femur or tibia reaches 380 Nm.
In the knee joint static certification test, the ends of the knee joint shall be mounted to the support rig firmly as shown in Figure 5.
In the knee joint static certification test, the Y-axis of the impactor shall be parallel to the loading axis within ±2° tolerance.
In the knee joint static certification test, a neoprene sheet shall be set underneath the loading ram and the impactor face of the knee joint described in Figure 3 of Annex 4 shall be removed.
The neoprene sheet used in the knee joint static certification test shall have compression characteristics as shown in Figure 2 (b) of Annex 5.
In the knee joint static certification test, the centre of the loading force shall be applied at the knee joint centre within ±2 mm tolerance along the Z-axis.

In the knee joint static certification test, the external load shall be increased so as to maintain a deflection rate between 10 and 100 mm/minute until the bending moment at the centre part of the knee joint (Mc) reaches 400 Nm.
The test facility used for the flexible lower legform pendulum certification test shall have a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 2 °C during the test.
The temperature of the certification area for the flexible lower legform pendulum certification test shall be measured at the time of certification and recorded in a certification report.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-1 shall be 235 Nm ≤ 272 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-2 shall be 187 Nm ≤ 219 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-3 shall be 139 Nm ≤ 166 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-4 shall be 90 Nm ≤ 111 Nm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum MCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 20.5 ≤ 24.0 mm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum ACL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 8.0 mm ≤ 10.5 mm.
In the pendulum certification test, the absolute value of the maximum PCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 3.5 mm ≤ 5.0 mm.
For the pendulum certification test maximum bending moment and maximum elongation values, the readings used shall be from the initial impact timing to 200 ms after the impact timing.
In the pendulum certification test, the instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers.
In the pendulum certification test, the CAC response values, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations and 400 Nm for the tibia bending moments.

In the pendulum certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor, including the flesh and skin, shall be suspended from the dynamic certification test rig 15° ± 1° upward from the horizontal as shown in Figure 6.
In the pendulum certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor shall be released from the suspended position and fall freely against the pin joint of the test rig.
In the pendulum certification test, the knee joint centre of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 30 mm ± 1 mm below the bottom line of the stopper bar when the impactor is hanging freely.
In the pendulum certification test, the tibia impact face without the flesh and skin shall be located 13 mm ± 2 mm from the front upper edge of the stopper bar when the impactor is hanging freely.
The test facility used for the flexible lower legform inverse certification test shall have a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 2 °C during the test.
The temperature of the certification area for the flexible lower legform inverse certification test shall be measured at the time of certification and recorded in a certification report.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-1 shall be 230 Nm ≤ 272 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-2 shall be 210 Nm ≤ 252 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-3 shall be 166 Nm ≤ 192 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum bending moment of the flexible lower legform impactor at Tibia-4 shall be 93 Nm ≤ 108 Nm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum MCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 17.0 ≤ 21.0 mm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum ACL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 8.0 mm ≤ 10.0 mm.
In the inverse certification test, the absolute value of the maximum PCL elongation of the flexible lower legform impactor shall be 4.0 mm ≤ 6.0 mm.
For the inverse certification test maximum bending moment and maximum elongation values, the readings used shall be from the initial impact timing to 50 ms after the impact timing.
In the inverse certification test, the instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all transducers.
In the inverse certification test, the CAC response values, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 30 mm for the knee ligament elongations and 400 Nm for the tibia bending moments.
In the inverse certification test, the assembled flexible lower legform impactor (with the flesh and skin) shall be hung vertically and freely suspended from a test rig as shown in Figure 7.

In the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor is impacted by the upper edge of a linearly guided aluminium honeycomb impactor, covered by a thin paper cloth with a maximum thickness of 1 mm, at an impact speed of 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
In the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor shall achieve a free flight condition within 10 ms after the time of first contact of the honeycomb impactor.
The 5052 alloy honeycomb attached in front of the moving ram for the inverse certification test shall be 200 mm ± 5 mm wide, 160 mm ± 5 mm high and 60 mm ± 2 mm deep.
The honeycomb for the inverse certification test shall have a crush strength of 75 pound per square inch (psi) ±10 per cent.
The honeycomb for the inverse certification test should have cell sizes of either 3/16 inch or ¼ inch and a density of 2.0 pcf for the 3/16 inch cell size or 2.3 pcf for the ¼ inch cell size.
In the inverse certification test, the upper edge of the honeycomb face shall be in line with the rigid plate of the linearly guided impactor.

At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the upper edge of the honeycomb shall be in line with the knee joint centre line of the flexible lower legform impactor within a vertical tolerance of ±2 mm.
The honeycomb shall not be deformed before the inverse certification impact test.

At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor pitch angle (rotation around the Y-axis), and therefore the pitch angle of the velocity vector of the honeycomb impactor, shall be within a tolerance of ±2° in relation to the lateral vertical plane.

At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor roll angle (rotation around the X-axis), and therefore the roll angle of the honeycomb impactor, shall be within a tolerance of ±2° in relation to the longitudinal vertical plane.

At the time of first contact in the inverse certification test, the flexible lower legform impactor yaw angle (rotation around the Z-axis), and therefore the yaw angle of the velocity vector of the honeycomb impactor, shall be within a tolerance of ±2°.
The certified upper legform impactor may be used for a maximum of 20 impacts before re-certification (this limit does not apply to propulsion or guidance components).
The upper legform impactor shall be re-certified if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification.
condition: if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification

text: The upper legform impactor shall be re-certified if any impactor transducer output, in any impact, has exceeded the specified CAC.
condition: if any transducer output has exceeded the specified CAC

text: The foam flesh for the upper legform test impactor shall be stored for a period of at least four hours in a controlled storage area with a stabilized humidity of 35 ± 10 per cent and a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 2 °C prior to impactor removal for certification.
The upper legform test impactor itself shall have a temperature of 20 °C ± 2 °C at the time of impact during certification.
The temperature tolerances for the upper legform test impactor shall apply at a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 per cent after a soak period of at least four hours prior to their application in a test.
The test facility used for the upper legform impactor certification test shall have a stabilized humidity of 40 ± 30 per cent during certification.
The test facility used for the upper legform impactor certification test shall have a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C during certification.
Each upper legform impactor certification shall be completed within two hours of when the impactor to be calibrated is removed from the controlled storage area.
The relative humidity and temperature of the upper legform impactor certification area shall be measured at the time of certification and recorded in the certification report.
When the upper legform impactor is propelled into a stationary cylindrical pendulum, the peak force measured in each load transducer shall be not less than 1.20 kN and not more than 1.55 kN.
In the upper legform impactor pendulum certification, the difference between the peak forces measured in the top and bottom load transducers shall not be more than 0.10 kN.
In the upper legform impactor pendulum certification, the peak bending moment measured by the strain gauges on the centre position shall not be less than 190 Nm and not more than 250 Nm.
In the upper legform impactor pendulum certification, the peak bending moment measured by the strain gauges for the outer positions shall not be less than 160 Nm and not more than 220 Nm.
In the upper legform impactor pendulum certification, the difference between the upper and lower peak bending moments shall not be more than 20 Nm.
For all upper legform certification force and bending moment values, the readings used shall be from the initial impact with the pendulum and not from the arresting phase.
Any system used to arrest the upper legform impactor or pendulum shall be so arranged that the arresting phase does not overlap in time with the initial impact.
condition: if an arresting system is used

text: The arresting system shall not cause the upper legform impactor transducer outputs to exceed the specified CAC.
condition: if an arresting system is used

text: The instrumentation response value CFC, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 180 for all upper legform impactor transducers in the certification test.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 10 kN for the upper legform impactor force transducers in the certification test.
The CAC response value, as defined in ISO 6487:2002, shall be 1,000 Nm for the upper legform impactor bending moment measurements in the certification test.
For certification, the upper legform impactor shall be mounted to the propulsion and guidance system by a torque limiting joint.
The torque limiting joint shall be set so that the longitudinal axis of the upper legform front member is perpendicular to the axis of the guidance system, with a tolerance of ±2°.
The torque limiting joint friction torque shall be set to 675 Nm ± 25 Nm for the upper legform impactor certification.
The guidance system shall be fitted with low friction guides that allow the upper legform impactor to move only in the specified direction of impact when in contact with the pendulum.

The upper legform impactor mass shall be adjusted to give a mass of 12 kg ± 0.1 kg for certification, including those propulsion and guidance components which are effectively part of the impactor during impact.

The centre of gravity of those parts of the upper legform impactor effectively forward of the torque limiting joint, including the extra masses fitted, shall lie on the longitudinal centreline of the impactor with a tolerance of ±10 mm.
The upper legform impactor shall be certified with previously unused foam.
The upper legform impactor foam shall not be excessively handled or deformed before, during or after fitting.
The upper legform impactor with the front member vertical shall be propelled horizontally at a velocity of 7.1 m/s ± 0.1 m/s into the stationary pendulum.
The certification pendulum tube shall have a mass of 3 kg ± 0.03 kg.
The certification pendulum tube shall have a wall thickness of 3 mm ± 0.15 mm.
The certification pendulum tube shall have an outside diameter of 150 mm +1 mm/-4 mm.
The total certification pendulum tube length shall be 275 mm ± 25 mm.

The certification pendulum tube shall be made from cold finished seamless steel (metal surface plating is permissible for protection from corrosion), with an outer surface finish of better than 2.0 micrometer.
The certification pendulum tube shall be suspended on two wire ropes of 1.5 mm ± 0.2 mm diameter and of 2.0 m minimum length.
The surface of the certification pendulum shall be clean and dry.
The pendulum tube shall be positioned so that the longitudinal axis of the cylinder is perpendicular to the upper legform front member (i.e. level), with a tolerance of ±2℃.
The pendulum tube shall be positioned so that the longitudinal axis of the cylinder is perpendicular to the direction of upper legform impactor motion, with a tolerance of ±2℃.
The centre of the pendulum tube shall be aligned with the centre of the upper legform impactor front member, with tolerances of ±5 mm laterally and ±5 mm vertically.
The certified child and adult headform impactors may be used for a maximum of 20 impacts before re-certification.
The child and adult headform impactors shall be re-certified if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification.
condition: if more than one year has elapsed since the previous certification

text: The child and adult headform impactors shall be re-certified if the transducer output, in any impact, has exceeded the specified CAC.
condition: if the transducer output has exceeded the specified CAC

text: When dropped from a height of 376 mm ± 1 mm in accordance with paragraph 3.3, the peak resultant acceleration measured in the child headform impactor shall be not less than 245 g and not more than 300 g.

When dropped from a height of 376 mm ± 1 mm in accordance with paragraph 3.3, the peak resultant acceleration measured in the adult headform impactor shall be not less than 225 g and not more than 275 g.
The acceleration time curve of the headform impactor in the drop test shall be uni-modal.
The instrumentation response value CFC for each headform accelerometer in the drop test shall be 1,000 Hz as defined in ISO 6487:2002.
The instrumentation response value CAC for each headform accelerometer in the drop test shall be 500 g as defined in ISO 6487:2002.
The headform impactors shall have a temperature of 20 °C ± 2 °C at the time of impact in the drop test.
The headform impactor temperature tolerances shall apply at a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 per cent after a soak period of at least four hours prior to their application in a test.
The headform impactor shall be suspended from a drop rig as shown in Figure 9.
The headform impactor shall be dropped from the specified height by means that ensure instant release.

The headform impactor shall be dropped onto a rigidly supported flat horizontal steel plate, over 50 mm thick and over 300 mm x 300 mm square, which has a clean dry surface and a surface finish of between 0.2 and 2.0 micrometer.
The child headform impactor shall be dropped with the rear face of the impactor at the test angle specified in Annex 5, paragraph 4.7. with respect to the vertical.
The adult headform impactor shall be dropped with the rear face of the impactor at the test angle specified in Annex 5, paragraph 5.7. with respect to the vertical.
The suspension of the headform impactor shall be such that it does not rotate during the fall.
The headform drop test shall be performed three times, with the headform impactor rotated 120° around its symmetrical axis after each test.
